pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING ALOUD: FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.3: Reading Aloud: Fluency

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading Aloud: Fluency. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to read correctly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use appropriate speed to read simple texts for fluency

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING ALOUD: FLUENCY
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading Aloud: Fluency helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING ALOUD: FLUENCY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use appropriate speed to read simple texts for fluency

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate speed to read simple texts for fluency. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate speed to read simple texts for fluency.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Aloud: Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate speed to read simple texts for fluency. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading Aloud: Fluency is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Aloud: Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use appropriate speed to read simple texts for fluency)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading Aloud: Fluency to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use appropriate speed to read simple texts for fluency.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading Aloud: Fluency from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading Aloud: Fluency: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Reading Aloud: Fluency?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to read correctly?
2. How does reading speed enhance fluency?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading Aloud: Fluency means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use appropriate speed to read simple texts for fluency.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
